records.source: מִזְמ֗וֹר לְדָ֫וִ֥דיְ֭הֹוָה מִי־יָג֣וּר בְּאָהֳלֶ֑ךָ מִֽי־יִ֝שְׁכֹּ֗ן בְּהַ֣ר קָדְשֶֽׁךָ׃
records.gloss: A psalm of David. YHWH, who may sojourn in your tent? Who may dwell on [the] mountain of your holiness?
pieces: A psalm of David. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, who may stay as a guest in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} tent? Who may make a home on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy mountain?

L.1: A psalm of David. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, who may sojourn in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} tent? Who may dwell on the mountain of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holiness?

R.1: A song of David. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, who is welcome to stay with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} tent? Who can live on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy hill?

decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.
The verb (gur) is used of someone who lives in a place not their own, as a guest under the protection of the host (5:5; 61:5).

decisions.choice: your tent, your holy mountain: the place of worship on Zion
decisions.reason: The tent is the shelter David set up for the ark on Mount Zion (2 Samuel 6:17); the holy mountain is Zion (2:6).

decisions.choice: Who may ...?: a question at the gate
decisions.reason: The psalm asks who may come into God's presence and answers with a description of a life, as Psalm 24:3-6 and Isaiah 33:14-16 do.

records.heading: Who may stay in God's tent?

records.source: הוֹלֵ֣ךְ תָּ֭מִים וּפֹעֵ֥ל צֶ֑דֶק וְדֹבֵ֥ר אֱ֝מֶ֗ת בִּלְבָבֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: [One who] walks blameless and does righteousness and speaks truth in his heart,
pieces: Whoever walks without blame, practices what is right, and speaks truth that comes from the heart,

L.2: [One who] walks blameless and does righteousness and speaks truth in {{gender:their|his}} heart,

R.2: It is the person who lives a good life and does what is right. That person tells the truth and means it.

decisions.reason: The word (tamim) means whole or sound: a life with integrity, not a life without any fault (Genesis 6:9; 17:1).

decisions.choice: speaks truth in his heart: truthful through and through
decisions.reason: The truth is in the heart as well as on the lips; such a person does not say one thing and mean another (12:3).
The answer to verse 1 runs from here to the middle of verse 5, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.
The person described is anyone who lives this way.

records.source: לֹֽא־רָגַ֨ל׀עַל־לְשֹׁנ֗וֹ לֹא־עָשָׂ֣ה לְרֵעֵ֣הוּ רָעָ֑ה וְ֝חֶרְפָּ֗ה לֹא־נָשָׂ֥א עַל־קְרֹֽבוֹ׃
records.gloss: [who] has not gone about on his tongue, has not done to his neighbor evil, and reproach has not taken up against his near one,
pieces: who does not go around spreading slander, does no harm to a neighbor, and does not heap insults on those close by,

L.3: [who] does not go about on {{gender:their|his}} tongue, does not do evil to {{gender:their|his}} neighbor, and does not take up reproach against {{gender:their|his}} near one,

R.3: That person does not tell lies about others or hurt a neighbor or say cruel things about people nearby.

decisions.choice: go about on his tongue: slander
decisions.reason: The verb (ragal) comes from the word for foot: to go about from one person to another with gossip and slander (Leviticus 19:16 uses a related word).

decisions.choice: take up reproach: speak or spread insults
alternatives: put up with insults against a neighbor
decisions.reason: To take up a reproach is most likely to raise it, casting shame on someone near; it could also mean to accept or repeat a shameful story about them.

records.source: נִבְזֶ֤ה׀בְּֽעֵ֘ינָ֤יו נִמְאָ֗ס וְאֶת־יִרְאֵ֣י יְהוָ֣ה יְכַבֵּ֑ד נִשְׁבַּ֥ע לְ֝הָרַ֗ע וְלֹ֣א יָמִֽר׃
records.gloss: despised in his eyes [is] a rejected [one], but those who fear YHWH he honors; he swears to do harm and does not change.
pieces: who looks with contempt on one who is rejected but shows honor to all who fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and who stands by a sworn promise at personal cost, never going back on it.

L.4: in whose eyes one rejected [is] despised, but who honors those who fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; who swears to do harm and does not change.

R.4: Such a person looks down on those whom God has rejected but respects people who honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. When they make a promise, they keep it, even when it costs them a lot.

decisions.choice: a rejected one: someone God has rejected
decisions.reason: The word (nim'as) means rejected, here most likely one who has been rejected by God for his wickedness (1 Samuel 15:23). The godly person does not admire such people, however powerful they are.

decisions.choice: swears to do harm and does not change: keeps an oath though it hurts
alternatives: swears to his neighbor (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The words "swears to do harm" most likely mean making a promise that turns out to cost the one who made it, and keeping it anyway (Leviticus 5:4 speaks of swearing "to do harm or to do good"). The ancient Greek translation reads "swears to his neighbor".
Readable names who has rejected them (m1).

records.source: כַּסְפּ֤וֹ׀לֹא־נָתַ֣ן בְּנֶשֶׁךְ֮ וְשֹׁ֥חַד עַל־נָקִ֗י לֹ֥א לָ֫קָ֥ח עֹֽשֵׂה־אֵ֑לֶּה לֹ֖א יִמּ֣וֹט לְעוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: his money he has not given at interest, and a bribe against [the] innocent he has not taken. [One who] does these will not be shaken forever.
pieces: who does not lend money to make a profit from interest, and will not take a bribe to harm the innocent. Anyone who lives like this will stand firm forever.

L.5: who does not give {{gender:their|his}} money at interest, and does not take a bribe against [the] innocent. [One who] does these [things] will not be shaken forever.

R.5: That person does not charge interest when lending money, and does not take money to hurt people who have done nothing wrong. Anyone who lives this way will always be safe and secure.

decisions.choice: money at interest: profit taken from the needy
decisions.reason: God's law forbade Israelites to charge interest on loans to a fellow Israelite in need (Leviticus 25:35-37); lending was to help, not to profit from someone's trouble.

decisions.choice: a bribe against the innocent: paid to condemn them
decisions.reason: A bribe twisted justice in court (Exodus 23:8; Deuteronomy 16:19); here it is taken to bring down someone innocent.

decisions.choice: will not be shaken: will stand firm
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the psalmist's fear in 13:5; the one who lives this way will never be overthrown.
